ruling.recommended_action: Send case file to a human reviewer for the SAFE-1 safety screen on F12 before the $5.00 cancellation fee is finalised; do not execute the NS-1 outcome until the safety review is complete. In the interim Ryde ops may apply an interim_suspension to the accused driver pending review (SAFE-4). If no safety violation is found, the NS-1 conditions (i)–(iv) are satisfied and the $5.00 fee on record stands.
ruling.reasoning:
The dispute is a no-show cancellation charge: the driver cancelled at 17:15:30 with app reason rider_no_show [F4]. Under NS-0 the branch turns on who cancelled and why, and the app reason is only the driver's claim [F4]; his own words are “I waited more than 5 minutes and called. The rider said 2 minutes and never came. I cancelled as a no-show” [F15] — no reason of his own (no car trouble, personal matter, other job, refusal), so on NS-0's reading the ground is rider no-show, not NS-3.

The NS-1 conditions are settled by the records: arrival was confirmed by the driver's tap at 17:10:00, 40 m from the pickup and within 200 m (closest approach 38 m) [F7][F1]; he stayed at the pickup 330 s continuously from arrival, past the ≥ 5-minute free wait [F7][F3]; before cancelling he sent 2 in-app messages (first 17:10:30) and made 1 in-app call (17:11:30) [F5][F10][F14]; he remained within 200 m throughout [F2][F7]. The rider answered “2 min, coming” at 17:12 [F11] and did not appear. On those records the $5.00 fee on record [F8] would stand under NS-1, and NS-9 is not triggered — no prior no-show on record [F19].

The case cannot be ruled here, however, because of the safety screen. Message #3 at 17:15 — “Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it.” [F12] — is read in context: it is not a pickup arrangement or a route remark; coming from the driver to the rider after she said she was two minutes away [F11], it is an intimidatory statement directed at the rider, and the rider's complaint alleges the driver “threatened me” [complaint]. That is at least a suspected case under SAFE-1 (§5.2 – threats/intimidation flagged for immediate human escalation, regardless of dispute type), and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F13], so the screen rests on a readable message, not an inference.

Because the screen is suspected, I must not rule on the merits or assign fault (SAFE-3, §5.2); the human reviewer decides whether the fee stands and whether any account action follows. The summary for that reviewer: rider booked Bugis Junction → Jurong East MRT (accepted 17:08:00), driver tapped “I'm Here” at 17:10:00 40 m from the pickup [F7], waited 5 min 30 s [F3], messaged and called [F5][F14], rider replied “2 min, coming” at 17:12 [F11], driver cancelled at 17:15:30 for rider_no_show after sending the message at F12 [F4]; the $5.00 fee was charged [F8]. Points to check: the intent and impact of F12, and whether the NS-1 no-show conditions, which the code settles as met, are to be applied to the fee once the safety review concludes. No traffic cause is relevant to the NS-1 analysis [F16][F17]; the profiles [F19][F20] do not decide anything.

element_findings.reason: The app reason is rider_no_show [F4] and the driver's own message and written statement give no reason of his own — he says he waited over 5 minutes, called, the rider said 2 minutes and never came, so he cancelled as a no-show [F10][F12][F15]. That is the NS-1 branch, not NS-3.

Read in context, the driver's message “Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it.” [F12], sent after the rider's “2 min, coming” [F11], is an intimidatory statement aimed at the rider and supports the complaint's threat allegation; SAFE-1 (§5.2) requires human escalation.
